text: The proposed 30-day compliance window for Clause 7 is severely burdensome for seed-stage startups. We strongly suggest extending the transition period to at least 180 days with a phase-in approach.

While mandatory algorithmic audits are commendable, there is serious concern regarding the leakage of proprietary intellectual property. We recommend establishing independent certified audit frameworks.
We wholeheartedly welcome the requirement in Clause 15 for a 48-hour acknowledgment of consumer complaints to strengthen consumer protection.

Clause 3 mandates strict local storage of all transaction metadata. This will exponentially escalate infrastructure costs for cloud-native firms. We recommend adopting a risk-based data categorization framework.
The proposed penalty of up to 4% of global turnover is disproportionately punitive for procedural lapses. We advise introducing a statutory cure notice period of 45 days.
This draft submission is filed for general consultation regarding standard clause definitions without specific objections.
Cross-border data flows are the backbone of SaaS exporters. We recommend aligning cross-border adequacy rules with recognized international standards like ISO/IEC.
Local data storage is vital to protect citizen data. We fully support Clause 3 and recommend strict non-waivable penalties.
Requiring dedicated round-the-clock grievance officers is impractical for early-stage fintechs. We propose allowing pooled industry ombudsman services for startups.
Clause 12 lacks precise technical definitions of algorithmic bias which creates legal ambiguity for developers.
